cell-ledger close (hauska-engine PR #377, merged) confirmed as the source of evaluatePublishGate/loadCountyParcelRecords -- read both files directly at packages/engine-core/src/parcel-record/{publish-gate,load}.ts.

The 101.5s smallest-county figure belongs to loadCountyParcelRecords, which always loads all 65 rails for every parcel in a county (load.ts's own doc comment: 'one county per call, always... never combine counties'). It is not itself rail-scoped -- consuming it as-is per rail would still pay the full-county cost 65 times over per county. This is the actual dead-end the dispatch's premise names, more precisely than 'materializing Travis' alone.

parcel_record_cell already carries the indexes a rail-scoped design needs: parcel_record_cell_rail_idx (rail_key) plus the PK (place_key, rail_key); parcel_record carries parcel_record_county_fips_idx. No migration needed to make a (county, rail) query fast.

designDecision.summary: Do not call the existing evaluatePublishGate/loadCountyParcelRecords for this card's per-rail evaluation -- they require a full ParcelRecordCells object (assertFullRecordCells enforces all 65 rail keys present), so a rail-scoped caller cannot construct a valid input without fabricating the other 64 rails, which would corrupt deriveLiveRailKeys'/deriveDeclaredAheadRailKeys' cross-record liveness computation for rails never actually loaded -- a sentinel-shaped violation of ENFORCEMENT.md's 'never satisfy a check with a sentinel', and it would misreport excludedDeclaredAhead (the mission's own item 2 names the exclusion set as part of the instrument's contract).
designDecision.chosen: Add a new, narrow rail-scoped instrument alongside the existing whole-county one, reusing the same underlying primitives (isEarnedCell/isUnaccounted from cell-state.ts) rather than reimplementing cell classification: loadCountyRailCells(sql, countyFips, railKey) (one county AND one rail per call, mirrors load.ts's existing one-county-per-call discipline) and evaluateRailGate(cells, railKey, options) (same ok/unaccountedCount/excludedDeclaredAhead/warnings shape as PublishGateVerdict, scoped to one rail). Liveness is naturally decomposable per rail -- deriveLiveRailKeys' definition of 'live' for a given rail (at least one earned cell of that rail, program-wide) does not depend on any OTHER rail's cells -- so this is a genuine narrowing of the same semantics, not a redesign.
designDecision.timingValidation: Live EXPLAIN ANALYZE against the smallest county (48055, flood rail): execution time 408.8ms (Gather node), vs the 101.5s full-65-rail load the dispatch's premise cites. The first cold connection took 11.8s wall-clock (network/SSL handshake, not query execution) -- the query itself is genuinely fast, not merely fast-looking on a warm cache. Confirms streaming/batching per rail is not just a theoretical fix for the named dead-end but a measured one order of magnitude (409ms vs 101,500ms) before any further optimization.
